case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 3rd day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J.: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 03.08.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006 discharging the Rule. 

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the appellant herein and others as plain-tiffs filed Other Class Suit No.131 of 1997 before the Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram for partition. They contended, inter alia, that the land described in the schedule to the plaint has been finally published in R.S. Khatian No.291 with the name of Anu Mia being an owner of the properties, who sold 44 decimal land to Ashu Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by registered deed No.724 dated 31.01.1954. The plaintiffs obtained total 58% decimal land and have been owning and possessing the suit land. The defendants have no right, title and interest in the suit land of the plaintiffs. On 19.09.1997 when the defendants denied to partition the said land from the jote, the cause of action arose and hence, the plain-tiffs filed the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos. l-4 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material averments made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest over the suit land. Moreover, the deed in question, which was registered on 04.02.1954 did not create any title in favour of the plaintiffs in the suit land because there is no similarly between the land in question in schedule No.1 to the plaint and the land described in the schedule to the deed. The defendants and their predecessor never sold the suit land to the plaintiffs' predecessor and the defendants have been in possession of the suit land, hence the plaintiffs' suit should be dismissed. 

4. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Patiya, Chattogram, by the judgment and decree dated 06.10.2005 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred Other Class Appeal No.565 of 2005 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chattogram. On transfer, the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chattogram, who by the judgment and decree dated 18.06.2006 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Then the plaintiffs preferred Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was discharged. Being aggrieved plaintiff No.1 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2044 of 2008 and leave was granted to consider the following grounds of the learned Advocate for the petitioner: 
"I. That the petitioner did not seek partition of the tank which is in Khatian No.202 in Plot Nos.124, 125, 131 and on receiving the written statement, made it clear by an amendment of the plaint that the tank has not been incorporated in the schedule of the plaint as it has been peacefully possessed by the co-sharers jointly and the appellate Court by misreading of those arrived at a finding that all the co-sharers have not been impleaded in the suit and observed “বিবাদী পক্ষে কথিত ২০২ নং খতিয়ানে ১২৪/১২৫/১৩১ দাগে ভূমি জলে পড়ে দিঘী। এখানে ২০০ জনের উপরে শরীক আছে। দিঘীর পরিমান ১০—কানি। আছু মিঞার অন্দরে ভূমি পরিমাণ ৩—গন্ডা বাকী সম জোতের উক্ত শরীকগণকে পক্ষ করেননি বলে অত্র আদালতে বিবেচনায় মূল মোকদ্দমা পক্ষভাবে দোষে দুষ্ট হবে।”and the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the fact that the finding of the appellate Court is perverse, which affected the merit of the case. II. That the appellate Court further observed in its finding that 
“বাদীপক্ষের স্বীকারোক্তি মতেই নালিশী ১৩২ দাগের ১৮ শতক ১১৫ দাগে ৪১ শতক ভূমি পুকুর শ্রেণী ভূমি। উক্ত পুকুর ভরাট না করে ভাগ বন্টন করা সম্ভব নহে—পুকুর শেনী ভূমি ভাগ বন্টনযোগ্য হওয়ায় মূল মোকদ্দমা ডিসমিস যোগ্য বটে। আমার এইরুপ সিদ্ধান্ত বসন্ত কুমার বনাম মতিলাল ১৫ সি.ডব্লিউ.এন ৫৫৫ এবং নিত্য গোপাল বনাম প্রানকৃষ্ণ সি.ডব্লিউ.এন ৪৩৯ মোকদ্দমা দ্বায়ের নজিরের উপর নির্ভরশীল” and the High Court Division committed an error of law not to interfere with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court as the finding is not based on the material evidence on record." 

5. This appeal was heard using virtual means under the provisions of the আদালত কর্তৃক তথ্য-প্রযুক্তি ব্যবহার আইন, ২০২০।

6. Mr. Abdus Sobhan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. In addition the learned Advocate submitted that the evidence on record itself speaks that one Anu Mia originally owned and possessed the property in schedule No.1 and the R.S. record of rights khatian No.291 was finally published, (Exhibit 2 Series) and the property of schedule No.2 also belonged to Anu Mia and others whose names appear in the R.S. record of rights finally published (Exhibit-2 Series) and who sold 44 decimals land to the predecessors of the plaintiff by deed No.724 registered on 04.02.1954 (Exhibit-3) and the plaintiffs produced B.S. Khatian No. 254 (C.C) and Asu Mia Majhi, predecessor of the plain-tiffs also purchased 141/3 decimals land by Exhibit-3 from Plot Nos.106/115/112 shown in schedule No.2 and in such a way the plaintiffs owned and are possessing 44 + 14 1/3 = 581/3 decimals land in both the schedules and sought partition and the High Court Division by misreading of those erroneously affirmed the finding of the appellate Court. He submitted that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and subsequently the plaintiffs themselves are in possession of the said quantum of land by virtue of the said sale deed (Exhibit-3) and the record of rights (Exhibit-2 series) on payment of usual taxes to the government, and in such circumstances the finding of possession of the, Court of first appeal was made through inadvertence and the High Court Division committed an error of law to give emphasis of the finding of possession of the Court on first appeal without considering the relevant aspects of possession. 

7. Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.1(a)-1(j) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He further submitted that the petitioner is entitled to 22 decimals land in 1/3rd share of 66 decimals land in the schedule No.1 to the sale Deed No.724 dated 04.02.1954, Ext3 and not 44 decimals land as claimed by the plaintiffs in the schedule No.1 to the plaint based on the schedule No.1 to the said sale deed and decree by the trial Court for 44 decimals in schedule No.1 to the plaint is erroneous. He also submitted that in schedule No.1 to the sale deed. No.724 dated 04.02.1954, Ext-3, on the basis of which the appellant has made his claim has specifically provided that “উক্ত বশত ভিটায় আপনার সাবেক দখালি ঘর দখল মতে থাকিবেন” and the appellant is not entitled to make extension of the dwelling house and possession in the homestead making contrary claim in the partition suit. He submitted that the quantum of the land to which the petitioner is entitled in schedule No.1 to the sale deed No.724 dated 04.02.19 54, Ext-3 has to be determined first in a properly framed title suit. The learned Advocate submitted that the judgment and decree of the trial Court is based on surmises and conjectures and the appellate Court has committed no error of law in allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit and the revisional Court has committed no error of law in upholding the judgment and decree of the appellate Court. 

8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

9. There was a claim and counter claim with regard to the fraction/share of land mentioned iii the schedule of deed No.724 registered on 04.2.1954. On direction from this Court the original volume containing the deed in question was transmit-ted to this Court by the (office of the District Registrar, Chattogram. On perusal of the volume and the deed in question, it transpires that the deed was created by Anu Miah Majhi, in favour of Asu Mia Majhi on 31.01.1954 and registered on 04.2.1954. The quantum of land sold is in total 58 1/3 decimals. Out of that lad, the disputed quantum of 44 decimals of R.S. Khatian No.291 is under the scanner. 

10. The first schedule of the deed reads as follows: 
“তপশীল (১) মৌংগৈড়লা থানা-পটিয়া মহল ২৪৫৯ নং তাং-রঘুরাম মতওলী মং মনিরুজ্জমা সওদাগর অধিনে আমার কায়মি রায়তি স্বত্ত্বীয় খাস দখল RS ২৯১/খং ১৩১/১৩২/১৩৩/ দাং পিছনের পুনি ও ১০১/দাং বশত বাড়ী ১/৩ অংশে মোং ৪০ শঃ ও ডেহরী ঘরের পশ্চিম ১০১/- দাং আং ১/২ অংশে কুড়িয়া তালা ভিটা মোং ৪শঃ মোট 8৪ শতক মং ২/১ আনা জমা সেস সহ উক্ত বশত ভিটায় আপনার সাবেক দখলি ঘর দখল মতে থাকিবেন।
 
11. The defendants claim that in the second schedule to the deed registered on 04.02.1954 the total land is 46 decimals of which the plaintiffs claim 1/3 that is 14 1/3 decimals. In the same way the predecessor of the defendants sold only 1/3 of the total land of khatian No. 291 that is 22 decimals out of total 66 decimals. Hence, the plaintiffs claim to title over remaining 44 decimals is false. 

12. We find from the deposition of P.W.1 that he claims that his predecessor purchased 13 decimals land from plot No.101 and 31 decimals land from plot Nos.131/132/133 which is correctly reflected in the 1st schedule of deed No.724. And the second schedule is in respect of 14 1/3 decimals land. But the record of rights wrongly shows a lesser quantum of land in the name of his father. The plaintiffs thus claimed saham for 58 1/3 decimals land. 

13. In his deposition defendant No.1 deposing as D.W.1 stated that in R.S. khatian No. 291 from plot Nos. 131, 132,133 and 101 his father sold only 1/3, i.e. 22 decimals by deed No. 724, and the plaintiffs have no claim to the remaining 44 decimals land. The trial Court accepted that the plaintiffs claim to title over 5873 decimals land is supported by the kabala Ext.3. On the other hand, the appellate Court observed that the schedule in the sale deed is self-contradictory because the plaintiffs' predecessor purchased only 'hot' the land detailed in the schedule 1 of the deed and, therefore, they could claim only 22 decimals land out of 66 decimals. It was also observed that in the B.S. khatian it is stated that the land sold is 1/3. The appellate Court also found defect of party and hotchpot. 

14. The High Court Division did not decide the issues regarding defect of party and hotchpot. But relied upon decisions of this Division to the effect that the findings of the appellate Court as the last court of fact are binding on the revisional, Court. However, the High Court Division did not consider the cited decisions of this Division where it has been held that a suit for partition will not be defeated for reason of defect of party and hotchpot. On the point of the quantum of land for which saham was claimed, the High Court Division followed the appellate Court's reasoning and held that the plaintiffs could not get saharn for 44 decimals in respect of '/3 Share of the plaintiffs' predecessor. 

15. We have scrutinised deed No.724. We may point out that the certified copy on record is same as the volume transmitted by the Registrar, Chattogram. We find that both the appellate Court and the High Court Division misread Schedule-1 of the deed. The reference to 1/3 share does not refer to the total quantum of land mentioned in that schedule but only to 1/3 of plot No.101 homestead. The reference to 40 decimals is the sun total of land of plot Nos. 131/132/133 plus 1/3 of the homestead of plot No. 101. In addition there is a further 4 decimals land of plot No. 101 to the west of the Dehari Ghar being 1/2 portion of "Kuria tala bhita". So, the land sold in the first schedule is neither 1/3 of 66 decimals nor 2/3 of 66 decimals as surmised by the High Court Division. 

16. In view of the above discussion, we find that the decisions of the appellate Court and the High Court Division are based on misreading of the schedule to the concerned deed of sale. 

17. The issues relating to defect of party and hotchpot are covered by the decisions of this Division as cited before the High Court Division. We need not revisit those here. 

18. Accordingly, we find merit in the appeal which is allowed, without however, any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order is set aside. The judgment and decree of the trial Court is restored. 

End.
